# Unsolicited POV Spec

Single source of truth for customer-specific POV documents — the visual one-pager and the accompanying outreach email. Based on deep research across RAIN Group, Corporate Visions, Gartner, Forrester, Challenger, and 2025-2026 cold outreach benchmarking data.

**Origin:** copied verbatim from `a local path` on 2026-10-15 so the
SCs gate the build in this repo. Retire the POV-project copy once this ships — two copies
will drift.

---

## Build scope for an internal issue — read this before claiming SC compliance

The 43 SCs below are not uniformly gateable, and pretending otherwise produces a false
pass. Three categories:

| Category | Count | How it is verified |
|---|---|---|
| **Machine-checkable** | ~21 | automated test — word counts, paragraph counts, link presence, absence of date stamps, em-dash count, single CTA, one-page render |
| **Judgment** | ~22, each already tagged `(non-testable)` in the list | human or model review. Record the reviewer's verdict; never auto-pass |
| **Out of scope for this build** | SC-13, SC-14 | sending behaviour, not generation |

**SC-13** (never send from primary domain) and **SC-14** (3-7-7 follow-up cadence) govern
how a human sends the result. This feature generates artifacts; it does not send mail.
Mark them `N/A — generator does not send`, do not mark them passed.

**SC-35** (Sapling < 50%, zero flagged sentences) *is* automatable — a Sapling AI-detection
integration exists and should gate the generated email before it is written to Drive.

**SC-43** (AE voice profile) has backing already: `src/ae-voice.ts` — `getVoiceProfile()`,
`detectVoiceProfile()`, `getVoiceTokens()`. Use it rather than reimplementing.

## What a POV Is

An unsolicited POV is a one-page visual document that demonstrates you understand a customer's current state, challenges, and strategic direction — then connects 2-3 of their initiatives as one interconnected decision. It earns credibility before the first meeting by showing homework, not a product pitch.

**POV = Convergence thesis + homework proof + one honest trade-off.**

The POV is attached as a PDF to a short outreach email. Together they form a package:
- **Email** — 75-125 words, sells the meeting
- **PDF** — visual, narrative, sells the forward ("thoughts?")

---

## THE EMAIL (15 rules)

### Structure (Rules 1-5)

1. **Provide both short and long versions.** Short version: 75-125 words (sweet spot per Boomerang, 40M emails). Long version: ~200 words max. Generate both so the AE can choose. Short is default recommendation — emails >200 words drop reply rates by 2.4x and 61% of B2B emails open on mobile.

2. **Three paragraphs, no more.** Personalized opener → value statement with a number → single clear CTA.

3. **Timeline hook, not problem hook.** Timeline-based hooks achieve 10.01% reply rates vs 4.77% for problem hooks — 2.3x difference (Digital Bloom 2025). Frame around compressed milestones, not pain.

4. **Single, specific, low-commitment CTA.** "Would October 15th work?" beats "Let's find time for a demo." Never Calendly on first touch. Never ask for more than 20 minutes.

5. **Reference the attached one-pager in one sentence.** "I've attached a short perspective on how [X], [Y], and [Z] intersect — one page." The email sells the meeting; the one-pager sells the forward.

### Content (Rules 6-10)

6. **Signal-driven opener, always.** Signal-personalized outreach: 15-25% reply rates vs 2-3% generic (Instantly 2026). The signal must be observable — never internal data.

7. **Share a distinct point of view, not product features.** 68% of decision-makers favor "sharing a distinct POV" over ROI tools (Corporate Visions 2026). Perspective sellers win 2.7x more deals.

8. **Correct a confident misunderstanding.** 69% of buyers seek seller validation because they sense their AI-generated research may be wrong (Gartner May 2026). Show the buyer something they believe is true that isn't, or connect dots they haven't connected.

9. **Named peer reference with concrete metric — varied per persona.** "Gates Corporation freed 50% of compute capacity for AI" forwards. "Leading companies improved efficiency" gets deleted. One company, one number, hyperlinked to the public case study URL from the Verified Case Study Registry below. The company name itself is the anchor text (`<a href="URL">Company Name</a>`). When sending to multiple personas, assign different references to each — never repeat the same case study across all emails.

   **Two claim classes, and they are not interchangeable.** A PEER claim names a company and attributes a metric to it; it must come from the Verified Case Study Registry, be named, and be hyperlinked. A BENCHMARK claim is industry research or a Red Hat measurement with no customer named; it is allowed with a visible source attribution and an entry in the approved-benchmark registry. **Anonymous peer references are banned** — the REFERENCE-ACCOUNT-C one-pager's "One Top-3 US bank modernized 3,000+ applications" is the shape to refuse: it reads as a peer claim, names nobody, and links nowhere, so the recipient cannot check it. Either name the company from the registry or drop the claim.

10. **3rd-grade reading level.** 36% more responses at simpler reading level (Boomerang, 40M emails). Short words. Short sentences.

### Voice (Rule 10b — new)

10b. **Use the AE's voice profile from the dashboard.** Every email must match the owning AE's established voice — tone, sentence structure, opener pattern, vocabulary level. The dashboard serves the profile at `/api/ae/{name}/style-guide`, and the generation endpoint applies it without being asked. If no profile exists, use the default humble-expert voice: direct, specific, no superlatives. Never generate emails in a generic tone when a voice profile is available.

     *The source matters as much as the rule.* This previously named a local
     path under `a local path`, which does not exist for anyone consuming
     the POV plugin — so the rule was unsatisfiable off this machine, and the
     endpoint that does serve the profile went uncalled. Verified live on
     2026-10-19: `GET /api/ae/:name/style-guide` returns 200. A rule with no
     locatable source is a rule nothing can satisfy.

### Anti-Patterns (Rules 11-15)

11. **Never spray-and-pray.** Narrowing ICP from broad to specific: 2% → 11% response (Belkins 2025).

12. **Never use AI to write the email.** Generic AI-written emails: 90% lower response rates. Use AI for research and signal gathering, not for writing. Run through Sapling; target <50% AI score. Avoid em dashes — they are a strong AI fingerprint in Sapling's token-level classifier. Use periods, commas, or restructure instead. Max one per email.

13. **Never send from primary domain.** Use separate lookalike domains for outbound to protect domain reputation.

14. **Never skip follow-up.** 48% of reps never follow up. First follow-up adds 40-50% more replies. 3-7-7 cadence captures 93% of total replies by Day 10.

15. **Never ask for more than 20 minutes on first touch.**

## THE ONE-PAGER / PDF (15 rules)

### Structure (Rules 16-20)

16. **One page, no exceptions.** The constraint is the feature — it forces prioritization and signals respect.

17. **200-350 words of copy, plus visuals.** Every word earns its place.

18. **Narrative arc: Environment → Insight → Convergence → Path Forward.** Mirror Challenger Commercial Teaching compressed to one page. Section vocabulary (REFERENCE-ACCOUNT-C — a design-vocabulary reference, not a format reference; see below): "Your Environment" → "What We're Seeing" → convergence callout → "The Numbers" → next steps.

19. **Convergence thesis as the centerpiece.** Connect 2-3 seemingly separate customer initiatives as one interconnected challenge. "These three threads are usually treated as separate conversations. We think they're the same conversation." Without convergence, 40%+ of deals end in "no decision" (CEB/Challenger).

20. **Bold key terms inline, and never an unsourced stat tile.** Running bold throughout body copy keeps the narrative in one piece, so carry the argument in prose rather than in a card grid. **Stat tiles are permitted** — the REFERENCE-ACCOUNT-C one-pager carries three, and they work — but every tile must print a visible source attribution on the tile itself: `40% TIMELINE REDUCTION (McKinsey, 2024)`, `12x→1x CPU CONSUMPTION (Red Hat benchmark)`. **An unsourced tile is forbidden.** The gate is one implication: tile present ⇒ attribution present. A bare number in a box is the easiest place in the document for an unverifiable claim to hide, which is why the attribution is the rule and the tile is not.

### Visual Design (Rules 21-25)

21. **Top-left entry, proof center, CTA bottom-right.** F-pattern reading. Headline at top-left, evidence in center, next steps at bottom.

22. **Logo/credibility signals over faces.** Partner logos, certification badges, named customer references build B2B trust faster than photos.

23. **Address both System 1 and System 2.** Even complex B2B decisions are 40% emotional (CEB/Gartner). Convergence callout = emotion; capability table = logic.

24. **Whitespace is functional, not decorative.** Generous spacing keeps decision-makers moving through the page.

25. **No date stamp, no file name in header/footer.** Must be forwardable weeks later without looking stale.

### Forward-Worthiness (Rules 26-30)

26. **Pass the "forward without changing a word" test.** Write from the buyer's perspective, in their language, with their metrics.

27. **Pre-answer exactly one objection.** One pre-empted objection = honesty; five = defensiveness.

28. **Specificity forwards, vagueness gets deleted.** Every claim must have a number or a named company.

29. **Honest about limitations.** One honest concession earns more trust than five superlatives.

30. **No gates.** No login, no form, no "contact us for details." Clean PDF that opens and forwards instantly.

---

## THE CONVERGENCE FORMAT (4 rules)

31. **Frame 2-3 customer initiatives as one interconnected challenge.** Not a product pitch with 3 bullets — a thesis that connects their world.

32. **Create a shared mental model.** The convergence callout (red-bordered box) is the most important element. It reframes how the buyer sees their own situation. This is the Commercial Insight from Challenger.

33. **Use a simple visual to show the connection.** Two-column diagram with the product connecting both initiatives (REFERENCE-ACCOUNT-C pattern: Project Redwood ← AAP → VMware Migration).

34. **Name their initiatives by name.** "Project Redwood" not "your modernization effort." Internal project names prove deep research.

---

## QUALITY GATES (6 rules)

35. **Sapling AI detection < 50%.** Zero flagged sentences. Run via `/humanize` skill.

36. **Creepy line check.** Never reference: support tickets, subscription counts, node counts, pipeline values, usage telemetry, layoff numbers.

37. **Competitor-swap test.** Replace product name with competitor's. If email still works, it's a brochure.

38. **One-page render test.** Print-preview the PDF. Any bleed to page two = tighten.

39. **Mobile render test.** Email must be fully visible without scrolling on mobile.

40. **Forward-worthy test.** Read the one-pager as the buyer's engineering lead receiving it forwarded with "thoughts?" — does it make sense without the email?

---

## Intelligence Requirements

Every POV must pull from these sources:

- [ ] DDB customer brief (if exists)
- [ ] Subsidiary/connected account briefs
- [ ] Web research: cloud migration, tech stack, leadership, hiring signals
- [ ] Leadership: CTO, CEO, target persona name + title + LinkedIn
- [ ] Existing Red Hat footprint (RHEL, Ansible, OpenShift subscriptions)
- [ ] Public case studies for peer reference (same industry preferred) — see Verified Case Study Registry below
- [ ] Regulatory/market hooks (SaaS tax, compliance, etc.)
- [ ] Target persona's own LinkedIn activity (posts, job history, skills)

## Verified Case Study Registry

**The registry is data, not prose. Source of truth: `config-templates/pov-case-studies.json`.**
Load it with `loadPovCaseStudies()` from `src/lib/pov-case-studies.ts` — never retype a
company, metric or URL from this document into a prompt or a generated artifact. Until
an internal issue the registry lived only here, nothing under `src/` could cite it, and the generator
filled the gap from model recall.

Match reference to persona by situation fit, not just industry. The table below mirrors the
seeded file for readers; if the two disagree, the JSON wins.

| id | Company | Industry | What They Did | Key Metric | Best For |
|----|---------|----------|---------------|------------|----------|
| `gates-corporation-openshift` | Gates Corporation | Manufacturing | 1,300+ VMs to OpenShift, 67 apps containerized, 5 clusters | 50% compute freed for AI | Scale + AI strategy |
| `b2-impact-openshift-virtualization` | B2 Impact | Financial Services | VM + container consolidation onto OpenShift Virtualization | 400 VMs → 150, 46 servers → 18 | Consolidation stories |
| `telefonica-brazil-openshift` | Telefónica Brazil | Telecom (116M customers) | Legacy virt to OpenShift production service bus | 99% faster scaling, 55% less CPU, 91% faster patching | Enterprise migration at scale |
| `reist-telecom-openshift-virtualization` | Reist Telecom AG | IT Services | Legacy virt to OpenShift, freed hardware became worker nodes | Licensing costs halved | Cost reduction |

**Registry URLs rot, and a rotted URL ships on a PDF to a customer.** The Telefónica Brazil
press release 404'd six weeks after being marked "verified as of 2026-10-01". The corrected
URL is in the JSON. Re-verification is a live HTTP check, not a reread:

```bash
POV_LIVE_URL_CHECK=1 bun test test/unit/pov-case-studies.test.ts
```

It is opt-in because the rest of `test/unit/` runs offline. It is proven able to fail:
repointing one entry at a nonexistent redhat.com path turns it red with
`404 https://www.redhat.com/en/resources/this-page-does-not-exist-1557`.

**Adding new case studies:** add an object to `config-templates/pov-case-studies.json` with
all eight fields, run the live check above, and set `verifiedOn` to the date it returned
200. Prefer named companies with concrete metrics — vague "leading enterprise" references
get deleted by recipients. Entries missing any required field are dropped by the loader
rather than half-cited.

## Validated Format Reference

**REFERENCE-ACCOUNT-C POV (Sep 2026) is a design-vocabulary reference, not a format reference.**
Take its visual and narrative vocabulary. Do not take its shape: it predates these rules
and **does not satisfy SC-16** (one page, no exceptions), so copying it produces a
document this spec rejects.

Measured against the artifact itself, not against memory of it — Drive
`a Drive file`, mirrored read-only to
`a local path — REFERENCE-ACCOUNT-C (Sep 2026).pdf`:

| Dimension | What the artifact actually is | Against this spec |
|---|---|---|
| Email | **111 words**, 3 tight bullets, "One-pager attached with the full convergence map" | inside SC-1's 75-125 band |
| PDF length | **approximately 2.5 pages** | **fails SC-16** — one page, no exceptions |
| Stat tiles | **three stat tiles, each carrying a visible source attribution** — `40% timeline reduction (McKinsey, 2024)`, `10x VM migration scale (AAP orchestration)`, `12x→1x CPU consumption (Red Hat benchmark)` | allowed under Rule 20 / SC-20: attributed, so not unsourced |
| Peer claim | "One Top-3 US bank modernized 3,000+ applications" — no company named, no link | **fails SC-9** — anonymous peer references are banned |
| Date stamp | "September 2026" in the header and the footer | fails SC-25 |
| Location | **Google Drive**, file id `a Drive file` | the artifact is **not** in the research vault; the vault holds the research write-up that produced these rules, not the PDF |

The email is a separate artifact from the PDF: Drive doc
`a Drive file`, "POV Email Draft — REFERENCE-ACCOUNT-C (Sep 2026)".
Its 111 words are a word-processor count of the body; a whitespace token count that drops
the three bullet glyphs and the three em dashes gives 110. The figure is tokeniser-
sensitive by a word either way, and the point it carries is not: this email sits near the
top of the 75-125 band, nowhere near the shorter length this section used to assert.

**Take from it:** the narrative arc ("Your Environment" → "What We're Seeing" →
convergence callout → "The Numbers" → "A Path Forward"), the red-bordered convergence
callout, the two-column `← AAP →` orchestrates-both diagram, the attributed tile row, and
bold-inline emphasis inside body copy.

**Do not take from it:** the page budget, the anonymous peer claim, or the date stamp.
For a one-page budget that already works, use
`a local path`.

Every row above is asserted in `test/unit/pov-spec-truth.test.ts`. The earlier version of
this section got the email length, the tile count and the location all wrong about the
file it pointed at, and the error survived because nothing read the two together (an internal issue).

## Success Criteria

Every criterion carries a class. The classes exist because "(non-testable)"
was never audited: it was applied to 22 criteria, and an internal issue found five of them
— SC-10, SC-17, SC-18, SC-30, SC-32 — to be ordinary arithmetic or string
searches. `.claude/rules/checks-must-be-able-to-fail.md` has a section on
exactly this: *"This cannot be checked" is a claim, and it is checkable.*

| Class | Meaning | Count |
|---|---|---|
| **MACHINE** (untagged) | checkable on the generated artifact alone | 25 |
| **GROUNDING** | checkable against the source data, not the text | 4 |
| **JUDGMENT** | human or model review; record the verdict, never auto-pass | 9 |
| **MOVED / MERGED** `[~]` | not the generator's to satisfy, or a duplicate id | 5 |

`[~]` ids are never reused and never deleted — a renumbered criterion silently
changes what a test that cites the old id is claiming.

**Merged:** SC-38 → SC-16 (both asked "is it one page?"), SC-42 → SC-15
(verbatim duplicate). Two deciders that agree are behaviourally one, and a
mutation of either leaves the other holding the case up.

**Moved to `docs/guides/pov-sending-runbook.md`:** SC-11, SC-13, SC-14. A
criterion the generator cannot affect can never go red for a true reason; it
can only be waived, which is tier F evidence, and it inflates the denominator.
